recommendation: Keep the fixed commit as-is. It is a narrow active-source consistency fix that implements the final FHIR-27544 interpretation without reopening the rejected proposal to require a $process-message return.
issue_request: FHIR-27544 was Applied as Not Persuasive with Modification for a concern that $process-message text contradicted messaging requirements about whether every request needs a response message. The final Jira comments and InM vote treated the already-applied messaging-page change to zero-or-more response messages as the modification, rather than requiring the $process-message return parameter to be 1..1.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly tagged FHIR-27544 was found. Commit 87b1af3c094d4dd726733409d815683ceeab15c7, tagged for FHIR-40518/FHIR-40519, changed the messaging introduction from one-or-more to zero-or-more response messages. Earlier published issues FHIR-25465 and FHIR-25252 clarified response-message expectations and $process-message empty-body responses.
additional_context: MessageHeader is active in source/fhir.ini and source/messaging.html is current messaging narrative source. The current source had the zero-or-more rule at the messaging introduction, but the $process-message narrative summary and OperationDefinition description still said one-or-more response messages, while the return parameter still called synchronous message returns mandatory. Zulip discussion and InM minutes confirm the intended direction was to remove the apparent every-message-response requirement.
reconciliation: Changed source/messaging.html and source/messageheader/operationdefinition-MessageHeader-process-message.xml so the $process-message summaries say zero or more response messages, and updated the return parameter documentation to make the synchronous response Bundle conditional on a needed response payload while preserving asynchronous no-return behavior.
source_changes: source/messaging.html: changed the $process-message narrative summary from returning one-or-more response messages to returning zero-or-more response messages.
source/messageheader/operationdefinition-MessageHeader-process-message.xml: changed the OperationDefinition description to zero-or-more response messages.

source/messageheader/operationdefinition-MessageHeader-process-message.xml: changed the return parameter documentation so a synchronous response message is present when a response payload is needed, not mandatory for every synchronous exchange.

related_jiras.note: Published the zero-or-more response-message wording that FHIR-27544 cites as the already-applied modification.
Established that message exchanges do not always require a response message and may be satisfied by HTTP-level acknowledgement.
Established that $process-message response content can be empty and that bare HTTP responses are valid in relevant cases.
Came from the same February 2023 messaging discussion and changed adjacent transfer-protocol wording in the same historical commit.
